title: The good and bad of peer pressure (SOP2)

sentences.en: When a new school year begins, students are dealing with classes, sports, and other extracurricular activities.
sentences.zh: 当新学年开始时，学生们要应对课程、体育和其他课外活动。

sentences.en: Most students will also face an entirely different set of challenges with peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 大多数学生还将面临一组完全不同的同辈压力挑战。

sentences.en: Parents may notice a change in how their child dresses or behaves at home.
sentences.zh: 父母可能会注意到孩子在穿着或在家里的行为上发生了变化。

sentences.en: How much of this is related to their friend's influence and how should parents address peer pressure with their children?
sentences.zh: 其中有多少与朋友的影响有关？父母又该如何与孩子探讨同辈压力？

sentences.en: In this podcast, we talk with a psychologist who looks at the science behind peer pressure, both the good and the bad.
sentences.zh: 在本期播客中，我们采访了一位心理学家，他探讨了同辈压力背后的科学，包括好的一面和坏的一面。

sentences.en: Brett Lowerson is a professor of psychology at Florida
sentences.zh: 布雷特·洛尔森（Brett Lowerson）是佛罗里达

sentences.en: Atlantic University, where his research focuses on how children and teens interact with their peers and parents.
sentences.zh: 大西洋大学的心理学教授，他的研究重点是儿童和青少年如何与同龄人及父母互动。

sentences.en: Specifically, he studies how these relationships affect their social lives and academics.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他研究这些关系如何影响他们的社交生活和学业。

sentences.en: Dr. Lowerson is a fellow of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 洛尔森博士是美国心理学会的资深会员。

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to speak with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能与您交谈。

sentences.en: When does peer pressure typically begin to occur in children's lives and what impact does it have on child and adolescent development?
sentences.zh: 同辈压力通常在儿童生活的什么时候开始出现？它对儿童和青少年的发展有什么影响？

sentences.en: Before we tackle that question, I think it's important to define peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 在我们探讨这个问题之前，我认为有必要先界定一下同辈压力的概念。

sentences.en: If we define peer pressure as essentially influence, then I think we can see that peer pressure begins very early on.
sentences.zh: 如果我们本质上将同辈压力定义为一种影响，那么我认为我们可以看到同辈压力的产生是非常早的。

sentences.en: But it's not often the way that parents and adults think of it.
sentences.zh: 但这往往不是父母和成年人所认为的那种形式。

sentences.en: You have explicit peer pressure and you have implicit peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 你有显性的同辈压力，也有隐性的同辈压力。

sentences.en: So let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: 所以我来举个例子。

sentences.en: I know of a young man who just started middle school and he started it with long hair.
sentences.zh: 我认识一个刚上初中的男孩，他刚入学时留着长发。

sentences.en: And a couple of months into middle school, he got his hair cut very short.
sentences.zh: 上了几个月初中后，他把头发剪得很短。

sentences.en: This could have been because somebody made fun of his long hair.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为有人取笑他的长发。

sentences.en: That would be the explicit form of peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 这就是显性同辈压力的形式。

sentences.en: But it could also be very implicit.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能非常隐蔽。

sentences.en: He could have wanted to fit in.
sentences.zh: 他可能只是想融入集体。

sentences.en: He could have been eager to make new friends, other kids with short hair and who didn't want, he didn't want them to be off put by his long hair.
sentences.zh: 他可能急于结交新朋友，比如其他留短发、不希望因他的长发而产生疏离感的孩子。

sentences.en: He could have thought this was some form of status that people with short hair appear to have more status than people with long hair.
sentences.zh: 他可能认为这是一种身份的象征，留短发的人似乎比留长发的人更有地位。

sentences.en: We don't know in this particular instance, and we often don't really know exactly if it's one or the other.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定的例子中我们不得而知，而且我们通常也无法真正确切知道到底是哪一种原因。

sentences.en: And typically, it's probably a combination of things.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，这可能是多种因素的结合。

sentences.en: So when we think about peer pressure, we're really talking about influence to behave differently.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考同辈压力时，我们实际上是在讨论改变行为的影响。

sentences.en: That's exerted by peers.
sentences.zh: 这种影响是由同龄人施加的。

sentences.en: So when does it begin?
sentences.zh: 那么它是什么时候开始的呢？

sentences.en: It begins as soon as children start to pay attention to what other children think about them.
sentences.zh: 它从孩子们开始关注其他孩子对他们的看法时就开始了。

sentences.en: So we can see peer influence in the very early grade school years.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在很小的学龄初期就能看到同龄人的影响。

sentences.en: We see it over behavior problems where one set of peers will influence another to act badly.
sentences.zh: 我们在行为问题上能看到这一点，当时某群同龄人会影响另一群人表现糟糕。

sentences.en: We also see it over academic achievement where friends do better when they're paired with other kids who are doing better in school.
sentences.zh: 我们也能在学业成就上看到这一点，当孩子们与在学校表现更好的其他孩子搭档时，朋友们的表现会更好。

sentences.en: And we've seen this in as early as first grade.
sentences.zh: 我们在一年级时就已经观察到这种现象了。

sentences.en: Our data in both
sentences.zh: 我们在

sentences.en: Finland and in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 芬兰和美国的数据

sentences.en: suggests that these influences happen with very young children.
sentences.zh: 表明，这些影响发生在非常小的儿童身上。

sentences.en: Why are some children and teens more susceptible to peer pressure than others?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些孩子和青少年比其他人更容易受到同辈压力的影响？

sentences.en: Because you see some kids that generally seem to just do their own thing and not care what other children think of them.
sentences.zh: 因为你会看到有些孩子通常只做他们自己的事，并不在乎其他孩子怎么看他们。

sentences.en: But that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非总是如此。

sentences.en: And why are some of them more susceptible to that?
sentences.zh: 为什么其中一些人更容易受到这种影响？

sentences.en: We're still working to
sentences.zh: 我们仍在努力

sentences.en: disentangle the notion of susceptibility from the notion of being really influential.
sentences.zh: 把“易受影响”的概念与“极具影响力”的概念区分开来。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, there are some children who are susceptible to influence from anyone, that is to say that
sentences.zh: 一方面，有些孩子容易受到任何人的影响，也就是说

sentences.en: whatever comes down the pike, they're likely to follow.
sentences.zh: 无论发生什么情况，他们都可能会盲目跟随。

sentences.en: But it's also the case that some people are more influential.
sentences.zh: 但同样的情况是，有些人更具影响力。

sentences.en: And so if you hang around with people who tend to be particularly influential, you will look susceptible, even though you're not particularly susceptible.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你和那些特别具有影响力的人混在一起，即使你本身并不是特别易受影响，你看上去也会像是易受影响的。

sentences.en: It just happens to be that you're hanging around with others who are highly influential.
sentences.zh: 这只是因为你刚好和那些极具影响力的人混在了一起。

sentences.en: So I'll try to address that
sentences.zh: 所以我会试着先处理

sentences.en: caveat out there first, because if you're hanging around with somebody who's very persuasive and who has a lot of social skills, you may look susceptible.
sentences.zh: 这个先决条件，因为如果你和一个极具说服力且社交能力很强的人混在一起，你可能会显得很脆弱。

sentences.en: In fact, you're not particularly susceptible to other people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你并不是特别容易受其他人影响。

sentences.en: It just has to do with those that you spend your time with.
sentences.zh: 这只与你花时间相处的人有关。

sentences.en: So we know that susceptibility is greater for children who don't have a lot of friends.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，对于没有多少朋友的孩子来说，易受影响的程度更高。

sentences.en: They want to protect the friendships that they have.
sentences.zh: 他们想要保护现有的友谊。

sentences.en: And so they're more likely to do what their friends say because they're worried about about losing their friends and have difficulty making others.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们更有可能听从朋友的话，因为他们担心失去朋友，而且很难结交新朋友。

sentences.en: Younger children who hang around with older children are susceptible to influence.
sentences.zh: 和较大孩子混在一起的较小儿童更容易受到影响。

sentences.en: Paradoxically, being popular may make you susceptible to influence.
sentences.zh: 矛盾的是，受欢迎可能会让你更容易受到影响。

sentences.en: This one is a little bit up in the air, but it may be that popular kids in some domains worry about protecting their status.
sentences.zh: 这一点还有待商榷，但可能是因为受欢迎的孩子在某些方面担心保护自己的地位。

sentences.en: And so they're more likely to be influenced, to be seen doing things that they should be seen doing, even if they don't want to do
sentences.zh: 因此，他们更有可能受到影响去做出“应该被看到”的行为，即使他们并不想去做

sentences.en: them, because otherwise they fear their status will diminish in the eyes of their peers.
sentences.zh: 这些事，因为否则他们害怕自己在同龄人眼中的地位会下降。

sentences.en: What about any difference between boys and girls when it comes to peer pressure?
sentences.zh: 在同辈压力方面，男孩和女孩之间有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: We don't have firm evidence on this, but I can tell you this much is for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们对此没有确凿的证据，但我可以告诉你，有一点是肯定的。

sentences.en: Boys spend much more time in groups than girls, whereas girls tend to spend their time in friendship diets.
sentences.zh: 男孩在群体中度过的时间比女孩多得多，而女孩往往在双人友谊中度过时间。

sentences.en: And so the influence that boys receive is much more likely to be concerned with fitting into the group as a whole.
sentences.zh: 因此，男孩受到的影响更有可能与融入整个群体有关。

sentences.en: And so boys need the approval of a larger group of peers, whereas girls are much more focused on getting along with one or another particular individual.
sentences.zh: 因此，男孩需要更大一群同龄人的认可，而女孩则更专注于与某一个特定的个人相处融洽。

sentences.en: And so we probably are going to see more individual influence on girls, whereas boys are going to be more apt to be susceptible to forces from the group as a whole.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会看到更多针对女孩的个体影响，而男孩则更容易受到整个群体力量的影响。

sentences.en: And I'm sure there are some parents that are listening to this wondering, what can they do to help children recognize and deal appropriately with peer pressure?
sentences.zh: 我确信有些父母听到这里会想：他们能做些什么来帮助孩子识别并妥善应对同辈压力？

sentences.en: It's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: The first thing I think that parents can do is that they can help children recognize that attempts to influence them are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我认为父母可以做的第一件事，就是帮助孩子认识到试图影响他们的尝试无处不在。

sentences.en: You can't turn around without somebody attempting to influence you.
sentences.zh: 你转过身就会发现有人在试图影响你。

sentences.en: They want you to eat this or buy that or watch this or listen to that.
sentences.zh: 他们想让你吃这个、买那个、看这个或听那个。

sentences.en: So one of the first things we can do is we can help children understand that our culture is full
sentences.zh: 所以我们能做的第一件事之一，就是帮助孩子理解我们的文化充满了

sentences.en: of influence attempts and peers are just another set of forces that are vying for our attention and are vying to shape our behavior.
sentences.zh: 各种影响尝试，而同龄人只是争夺我们注意力、塑造我们行为的另一股力量。

sentences.en: So once children start to see that there are these influences everywhere, that's really the first step in the process.
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦孩子们开始看到这些影响无处不在，这确实是整个过程的第一步。

sentences.en: So you recognize when there are influence attempts going on, and you can start to label them and recognize them and label them and recognize them.
sentences.zh: 所以你要在影响尝试发生时识别它们，并且你可以开始标记它们并识别它们，标记它们并识别它们。

sentences.en: And as children become more adept at recognizing and labeling them and identifying
sentences.zh: 随着孩子们越来越擅长识别、标记和确认

sentences.en: them, then you can start to talk with them about, you know, is that the kind of influence that you want to be shaped by?
sentences.zh: 它们，然后你就可以开始与他们讨论，你知道的，这真的是你想要塑造的那种影响吗？

sentences.en: Is that something that you want to be susceptible to?
sentences.zh: 这是你想去承受的影响吗？

sentences.en: And if not, then we start to talk about how we might resist that influence.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，那么我们开始讨论如何抵制这种影响。

sentences.en: But it's much easier to resist influence if you've thought about your strategies beforehand.
sentences.zh: 但是如果你事先考虑过你的策略，抵制影响就会容易得多。

sentences.en: If it's a teen going to a party and there's going to be somebody drinking there, is that something that you want to resist or not?
sentences.zh: 如果是一个青少年去参加派对，那里会有人喝酒，这是你想抵制的还是不想抵制的？

sentences.en: Certainly you want to tell your teen what are your strategies for if the person who was driving decides to drink?
sentences.zh: 当然，你想告诉你的青少年，如果开车的人决定喝酒，你有什么应对策略？

sentences.en: What are your strategies for not getting in the car?
sentences.zh: 你有什么策略不坐那辆车？

sentences.en: What is your strategy for finding a way home that won't involve driving with somebody who's been drinking?
sentences.zh: 你有什么策略能找到回家的路，而不需要坐喝过酒的人开的车？

sentences.en: So recognizing that there's influence out there, and it's not necessarily overt influence.
sentences.zh: 所以要认识到外界存在影响，而且这不一定是公开的影响。

sentences.en: There's going to be a lot of covert or of implicit influence, and that influence is just the same as all the other influence, and children need to be sensitive to that.
sentences.zh: 会有很多隐蔽或含蓄的影响，这种影响和其他所有影响一样，孩子们需要对这一点保持敏感。

sentences.en: Parents can serve as a buffer against peer influence.
sentences.zh: 父母可以充当抵御同龄人影响的缓冲区。

sentences.en: We know that children have good relations with their parents, feel that they have less of a need to please their friends.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，与父母关系良好的孩子，会觉得迎合朋友的需求没那么强烈。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example of one set of research findings that we have from work that we've done in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 我来举一个我们在瑞典开展的研究中的研究发现为例。

sentences.en: Children who have friends who are really burned out on school, who report that they are tired of school.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子的朋友对学校感到十分厌倦，他们报告说厌倦了学校。

sentences.en: If your friend is a high burnout on school, then you are much more likely to feel less interested in school.
sentences.zh: 如果你的朋友对学校有很高的倦怠感，那么你也会更有可能对学校失去兴趣。

sentences.en: School engagement is going to drop over the course of a year, unless you report really strong relations with your parents.
sentences.zh: 除非你报告说与父母的关系非常好，否则学校参与度在一年内会下降。

sentences.en: And so having a good relationship with your parents is going to buffer you against this adverse peer influence.
sentences.zh: 因此，与父母保持良好的关系将缓冲你免受这种不利的同辈影响。

sentences.en: Some of what you're talking about, a lot of what you're talking about is a negative peer influence, but some of your research has looked at how peer influence can be a positive
sentences.zh: 你所谈论的一些内容，你所谈论的很多内容都是消极的同辈影响，但你的一些研究探讨了同辈影响如何能成为孩子生活中的积极

sentences.en: factor in a child's life.
sentences.zh: 因素。

sentences.en: What are some examples of that, and what can children and teenagers do to develop these kinds of relationships?
sentences.zh: 其中的一些例子是什么？儿童和青少年可以做些什么来发展这些关系？

sentences.en: Well, if we think about it logically, it can't possibly be the case that all peer influence is bad, or else children would all inevitably end up as juvenile delinquents
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们合乎逻辑地思考，绝不可能所有的同辈影响都是坏的，否则孩子们最终都会不可避免地成为少年犯

sentences.en: because the influence would be negative and more negative and more negative, and everyone would be susceptible to it.
sentences.zh: 因为这种影响会变得越来越消极，每个人都会容易受到它的影响。

sentences.en: So there has to be some area of pushback.
sentences.zh: 所以必须有一些反弹的领域。

sentences.en: There has to be some area where peers are good.
sentences.zh: 必须有一些同龄人表现良好的领域。

sentences.en: We know that kids are going to be influenced for better or for worse by whoever is the more influential partner.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，无论好坏，孩子们都会受到更有影响力的伙伴的影响。

sentences.en: So if we take two friends, and we know that one is particularly influential, let's say the one who has more friend options, or the one who is older, or the one who's
sentences.zh: 如果我们挑选两个朋友，其中一个特别有影响力，比如说拥有更多交友选择的那个人，或者年龄较大的人，或者

sentences.en: doing better in school, or the one who's more attractive, whatever, the one who is more influential is going to set the tone for the influence.
sentences.zh: 在学校表现更好的人，或者更有吸引力的人，无论如何，更有影响力的人将定下影响的基调。

sentences.en: So if the one who is more influential doesn't like to drink, then we have data that suggests that actually teens desist from alcohol consumption, that the lower,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果更有影响力的人不喜欢喝酒，那么我们有数据表明，实际上青少年会停止饮酒，较低的

sentences.en: the less influential member of the group is going to desist from drinking because they want to be more like the more influential one.
sentences.zh: 群体中影响力较小的成员将停止饮酒，因为他们希望变得更像更有影响力的人。

sentences.en: We see the same thing that levels of delinquency will go down as well.
sentences.zh: 我们看到违法犯罪水平也会随之下降。

sentences.en: So it all depends on the characteristics of the more influential partner, and the same is true in a group.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都取决于更有影响力的伙伴的特征，群体中也是如此。

sentences.en: The group leaders.
sentences.zh: 群体领袖。

sentences.en: So the more that the group leaders have a positive agenda, the more that other children are more likely to be influenced by that positive agenda.
sentences.zh: 因此，群体领袖拥有积极议程的程度越高，其他孩子就越有可能受到该积极议程的影响。

sentences.en: So if you belong to a group where everybody's physically active, you're going to be physically active.
sentences.zh: 如果你属于一个每个人都积极进行体育锻炼的群体，你也会积极进行体育锻炼。

sentences.en: There's a big except for this,
sentences.zh: 这有一个重大的例外，

sentences.en: except for if you don't want to really, really don't want to do this, then you're likely to drop out of that group or not be friends with those particular individuals anymore.
sentences.zh: 除非你真的、真的不想这么做，那么你很可能会退出那个群体，或者不再与那些特定的人做朋友。

sentences.en: And you're going to go and select people who are more like you.
sentences.zh: 然后你会去寻找更像你的人。

sentences.en: And under those circumstances, when children are deselected from groups or drop out of friendships, then they go and look for kids who have more similar
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，当儿童被群体排除在外或退出友谊时，他们就会去寻找那些在饮酒或越轨行为上

sentences.en: levels of perhaps drinking or deviance, and then they may be inclined to be influenced in a different direction.
sentences.zh: 有着更相似水平的孩子，然后他们可能会倾向于朝另一个方向受到影响。

sentences.en: Does peer pressure follow people into adulthood, or is there a point in life when it becomes less of a factor?
sentences.zh: 同辈压力会伴随人们进入成年期吗？还是说生命中存在某个时间点，它会变得不那么重要？

sentences.en: For sure, peer pressure follows people across their whole life course, but you're going to receive it in different ways from different people.
sentences.zh: 肯定的，同辈压力会贯穿人们的一生，但你会以不同的方式从不同的人那里感受到它。

sentences.en: So do adults, are adults susceptible to peer pressure?
sentences.zh: 那么成年人，成年人容易受到同辈压力吗？

sentences.en: I think the answer is, of course.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: Last night, I went to back to school night for my children.
sentences.zh: 昨晚，我参加了孩子们的返校之夜。

sentences.en: And I was very impressed by the whole string of SUVs that arrived.
sentences.zh: 那一长串开过来的SUV给我留下了深刻的印象。

sentences.en: And out of the SUVs got moms with very similar haircuts and very similar length of heels and dads who all looked
sentences.zh: 从SUV里走出来的妈妈们留着非常相似的发型，穿着高度相似的鞋跟，爸爸们看起来

sentences.en: like they had gone shopping at the same place who differed only in terms of whether or not they wore a tie.
sentences.zh: 就像在同一个地方购物，唯一的区别在于他们是否系了领带。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All had the smartphones and the thing.
sentences.zh: 都拿着智能手机和那些玩意儿。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So there's no question that we're susceptible to peer influence and that this proceeds across the course of our life.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们容易受到同龄人影响，并且这种影响贯穿了我们的一生。

sentences.en: As we get older, we form romantic relationships, and we get married, then different peers influence us.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，我们建立恋爱关系，结婚，然后不同的同龄人影响我们。

sentences.en: But it's still peer influence, nevertheless.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，这仍然是同辈影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Lawerson.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您加入我们，洛尔森博士。

sentences.en: Pleasure was mine.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: For more information, please visit our website at apa.org slash speaking of psychology.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问我们的网站 apa.org slash speaking of psychology。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton with the American
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿（Audrey Hamilton），来自美国

sentences.en: Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 心理学会的“心理学访谈”（Speaking of Psychology）。
